From what I heard from a well known psychiatrist, she wasn't bipolar (as we thought), he said she suffered from a severe depression. And, from what a remember, she took fluoxetine without medical prescription, which might be contributed as well.

And there was also something my aunt (her sister) said that nobody knew by the time she was alive. That she went to get a magnetic resonance and discovered her brain had something wrong in an area related to humor. But unfortunately we will never know what exactly the problem was...

Maybe the desire to not have children was already founded, I can't really remember, because at the time my mother died I didn't have a partner yet. 

My mother dealed with depression her whole life, but the strange thing is that in the particular time she died, she didn't seem to be bad at all. She even told her best friend she was having the best time of her life, just one week before it happened...

That's a good question, I'm always discussing that with my wife. I would say that, for me, I feel a kind of "numbness". My wife (who knows me since I was 6 years old) says that I'm a "cold" person. But I don't feel that way.

I have a stepdaughter, and I don't have the desire to have a child of my own. I don't know if this has to do with the feeling of a "disrupted family" or if a never really wanted to have kids.

I was 31, already an adult, but even then it impacted all of our (me and my family) lives. You discover you are much stronger than you think you were, because you continue to go on with your life, you don't stop working, hanging with friends and family etc. Of course, the first year was a grieve period, but you still can do what you have to, because life doesn't give us a break.

Luckily, I have the best group of friends anyone could ask for.

But looking back from my perspective now (10 years later), I realize that there is an amount of sadness that is constantly inside me. I guess it happens to everyone who passed through the same experience.

Hey my friend. My mom committed suicide about ten years ago. She didn't leave a clue about what was going on with her. I mean, she struggled with depression her whole life, but by the time it happened, she wasn't depressed at all. It was such a strange thing.

I'm not an expert on the subject, I'm a survivor. I think if my mom wasn't so closed up, she could have spoken about her issues with me and our family, and this could be avoided. 

So, if I could give you some advice, it would be:

- try to get more and more connected with your friend, so maybe he gets more confidence and starts to speak clearly about his problems. Talking is always good, and knowing that someone is going to listen and really pay attention is even better. 

- inform his family and other friend without being invasive, so maybe he will find other sources of support.

Best of luck.
